S01.title: Wikipedia: Copenhagen
S01.quote: Bishop Absalon's construction of a modest fortress on the little island of Slotsholmen in 1167 … In 1254, it received a city charter under Bishop Jakob Erlandsen … by about 1416 Copenhagen had emerged as the capital of Denmark when Eric of Pomerania moved his seat to Copenhagen Castle … inaugurated on 1 June 1479 by King Christian I … a siege from July 1535 to July 1536 forced it to capitulate to Christian III … Copenhagen lost some 22,000 of its population of 65,000 to the plague in 1711 … On 2 April 1801, Parker's fleet encountered the Dano-Norwegian navy anchored near Copenhagen … In the early 1850s, the ramparts were opened to build housing around The Lakes … the districts of Nørrebro and Vesterbro developed to accommodate those who came from the provinces … from 120,000 in 1840 to 400,000 by 1901 … urban population of 1.4 million … Copenhagen harbour now has 13 official swimming zones and three harbour baths

S02.title: Wikipedia: History of Copenhagen
S02.quote: From June 1711 to March 1712, it was haunted by the plague which killed about a third of the population … During 1658-59 it withstood a severe siege by the Swedes under Charles X and successfully repelled a major assault … In 1901, Copenhagen expanded further, incorporating communities with 40,000 people … In August 1943, when the government's collaboration with the occupation forces collapsed, several ships were sunk in Copenhagen Harbour by the Royal Danish Navy to prevent them being used by the Germans … the extensive redevelopment of Amager … occupied by German troops along with the rest of the country from April 9, 1940, until May 4, 1945 … The crown succeeded in 1416, when Eric of Pomerania took over control of the town

S03.title: Wikipedia: Absalon
S03.quote: In 1167, Absalon was granted the land around the city of Havn

S04.title: Wikipedia: Christiansborg Palace
S04.quote: In 1370, King Valdemar IV of Denmark was defeated in a conflict with the Hanseatic League, who ordered the castle to be demolished … They sent 40 stonemasons to demolish the castle stone by stone … in 1733 work started on a magnificent baroque palace … Most of the palace complex was completed in 1745 and was the largest palace in northern Europe at the time … The palace and church were ruined by a fire in 1794 … Hansen started building the second Christiansborg in 1803 in a French Empire style … finished in 1828 … The second Christiansborg burned down in 1884 … The ruins remained in place for the following 23 years … which was built from 1907 to 1928 … at 106 meters became the tallest tower in the city

S05.title: Wikipedia: Børsen
S05.quote: Construction of the building began in 1620 and was largely completed in 1624 with the exception of the spire (installed in 1625) … spire, shaped as the tails of four dragons twined together, reaching a height of 56 m

S06.title: Wikipedia: Rundetårn (Round Tower)
S06.quote: The foundation stone was laid on 7 July 1637 … In 1642, the tower was finally completed … a 7.5-turn helical corridor leading to the platform at the top (34.8 meters above ground)

S07.title: Wikipedia: Rosenborg Castle
S07.quote: originally built as a country summerhouse in 1606 … finally evolving into its present condition by the year 1624

S08.title: Wikipedia: Frederik's Church (Marble Church)
S08.quote: popularly known as The Marble Church … The foundation stone was set by King Frederick V on 31 October 1749 … In 1770, the original plans for the church were abandoned by Johann Friedrich Struensee … sold the ruins of the uncompleted church and the church square to Carl Frederik Tietgen … The church was finally opened to the public on 19 August 1894 … the largest church dome in Scandinavia with a span of 31 metres

S09.title: Wikipedia: Amalienborg
S09.quote: laid around an octagonal courtyard … Building of the palaces on the western side of the square started in 1750 … after Christiansborg Palace burned in 1794 the royal family bought the palaces

S10.title: Wikipedia: Church of Our Saviour
S10.quote: did not start until 1682 … inaugurated 14 years later in 1695 … approved by the King in 1749 … Three years later the spire was finished and the King climbed the tower at a ceremony on 28 August 1752 … The black and golden spire reaches a height of 90 metres and the external staircase turns four times counterclockwise around it

S11.title: Wikipedia: Nyhavn
S11.quote: Nyhavn was constructed by King Christian V from 1670 to 1675, dug by Danish soldiers and Swedish prisoners of war

S12.title: Wikipedia: Tivoli Gardens
S12.quote: The park opened on 15 August 1843 … Until the 1850s Tivoli was outside the city, accessible from the city only through the Vesterport

S13.title: Wikipedia: Copenhagen City Hall
S13.quote: constructed between 1892 and 1905 … inaugurated on 12 September 1905 … at 105.6 metres

S14.title: Wikipedia: Copenhagen Opera House
S14.quote: It opened on 15 January 2005 … donated the Opera House to the Danish state in August 2000

S15.title: Wikipedia: Royal Danish Playhouse
S15.quote: With about 40 per cent of the building projecting over the water … RIBA European Award in 2008

S16.title: Wikipedia: Amager Bakke (CopenHill)
S16.quote: combined heat and power waste-to-energy plant … opened to the public 4–6 October 2019 … 85 meters tall sloped roof that doubles as year-round artificial ski slope

S17.title: Wikipedia: Øresund Bridge
S17.quote: Construction began in 1995 and it opened to traffic on 1 July 2000

S18.title: Wikipedia: Grundtvig's Church
S18.quote: on 8 September 1921, Grundtvig's birthday … leading to the initial inauguration of the so-called Tower Church in 1927 … continued until 1940 … reminiscent of a westwork or of the exterior of a church organ … 49 m (160 ft) tall bell tower

S19.title: Wikipedia: Royal Hotel (SAS Royal), Copenhagen
S19.quote: It was opened on July 1, 1960 … At 69.60 meters in height, it was the first skyscraper in Copenhagen

S20.title: Wikipedia: The Little Mermaid (statue)
S20.quote: unveiled on August 23, 1913 … It is 1.25 metres (4.1 ft) tall

S21.title: Wikipedia: Copenhagen Fire of 1728
S21.quote: It began on the evening of 20 October 1728 and continued to burn until the morning of the 23rd of October 1728 … It destroyed approximately 28% of the city … left 20% of the population homeless … No less than 47% of the section of the city, which dates back to the Middle Ages, was completely lost

S22.title: Wikipedia: Copenhagen Fire of 1795
S22.quote: started on Friday, 5 June 1795 … It had destroyed 909 houses and partially damaged 74 … Just over 6,000 of the just under 100,000 residents in the capital were made homeless

S23.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Copenhagen (1807)
S23.quote: On 2 September, the British began bombarding Copenhagen … the bombardment killed roughly 195 civilians and injured 768 … The bombardment included 300 Congreve rockets, which caused fires

S24.title: Wikipedia: Dano-Swedish War (1658-1660)
S24.quote: The Swedish army surrounded Copenhagen, hoping to starve it into submission … Charles then tried a decisive assault on the city, hoping to conquer it and win the war; this plan likewise failed … the assault of its capital on February 12, 1659 … When the Swedish invaded Zealand in August 1658

S25.title: Wikipedia: Kalmar Union
S25.quote: From 1397 to 1523, it joined under a single monarch the three kingdoms of Denmark, Sweden (then including much of present-day Finland), and Norway … Gustav Vasa's election as King of Sweden on 6 June 1523

S26.title: Wikipedia: Denmark-Norway
S26.quote: From 1536/1537, Denmark and Norway formed a personal union … in that year it became one of the most stringent absolute monarchies in Europe … formalized by an absolutist constitution, the King's Law … The Dano-Norwegian union lasted until 1814

S27.title: Wikipedia: Denmark in World War II (occupation)
S27.quote: On 9 April 1940, Germany invaded Denmark … German ships began disembarking troops at the docks in Copenhagen … which lasted until the Allied victory on 5 May 1945

S28.title: Wikipedia: Operation Carthage
S28.quote: Operation Carthage, on 21 March 1945, was a British air raid on Copenhagen … the raid caused 123 civilian deaths (including 87 schoolchildren and 18 adults at the school)

S29.title: Wikipedia: Freetown Christiania
S29.quote: On 26 September 1971, Christiania was declared open … It began in 1971 as a squatted military base

S31.title: Wikipedia: Constitution of Denmark
S31.quote: The first democratic constitution was adopted in 1849, replacing the 1665 absolutist constitution … Its adoption in 1849 ended an absolute monarchy and introduced democracy … Denmark celebrates the adoption of the Constitution on 5 June … The constitution defines Denmark as a constitutional monarchy

S32.title: Wikipedia: Hanseatic League
S32.quote: allied in the Confederation of Cologne in 1368, sacked Copenhagen and Helsingborg

S33.title: Wikipedia: Great Northern War plague outbreak
S33.quote: from June to November 1711, between 12,000 and 23,000 people died out of a population of ~60,000

S37.title: Wikipedia: Treaty of Kiel
S37.quote: further ceded the Kingdom of Norway to Sweden in return for Swedish Pomerania … on 14 January 1814 in Kiel

title: COPENHAGEN
1167 TO NOW

cards.title: Bishop Absalon's castle
lines: On a small island Absalon builds a fortress against Wendish pirates. A harbor town, Havn, grows around it.

cards.title: A city charter
lines: Bishop Jakob Erlandsen grants Havn a charter, backed by the local fishing merchants.

cards.title: København
lines: The name means "merchants' harbor": a town born from the harbor and trade.
cards.note: The 1303 year is the importer's placement only; S01 gives the etymology, not a date: shown without a date

cards.title: Hanseatic raid
lines: Hanseatic towns sack Copenhagen. They had attacked it again and again.

cards.title: Castle destroyed
lines: The Hanseatic League orders the king's castle torn down: 40 stonemasons take it apart stone by stone.

cards.title: Capital of Denmark
lines: Eric of Pomerania moves his seat to Copenhagen Castle. By about 1416 the city is the capital.

cards.title: A university
lines: King Christian I inaugurates the University of Copenhagen on 1 June 1479.

cards.title: A year-long siege
lines: From July 1535 to July 1536 the city holds out, then capitulates to Christian III. The Reformation of 1536 follows.

cards.title: Rosenborg Castle
lines: Christian IV builds a country summerhouse that grows into a Dutch Renaissance castle.

cards.title: Rosenborg Castle (1606)
lines: Rosenborg Castle (1606)

cards.title: Børsen
lines: A stock exchange topped by a spire of four dragon tails twined together.

cards.title: The Round Tower
lines: An observatory with no stairs: a 7.5-turn ramp climbs to the platform.

cards.title: The Swedish assault
lines: Sweden storms the besieged capital on 12 February 1659. The city holds.

cards.title: Absolute monarchy
lines: Denmark–Norway becomes one of the most stringent absolute monarchies in Europe. The King's Law of 1665 makes it official.

cards.title: Nyhavn
lines: Danish soldiers and Swedish prisoners of war dig a canal from the sea to Kongens Nytorv (1670-75).

cards.title: The plague
lines: The plague kills about a third of the people: some 22,000 of 65,000.
cards.note: S33 gives 12,000-23,000 dead of about 60,000: range, so "about a third"

cards.title: The Great Fire
lines: Three days of flames, 20-23 October. 28% of the city burns, 47% of the medieval part. 20% of the people lose their homes.
cards.note: Importer said 15,000 homeless: not in S21, replaced by 20% of the population

cards.title: Christiansborg
lines: Work starts on a baroque palace in 1733. Most of it is finished by 1745: the largest palace in northern Europe.

cards.title: Our Saviour's spiral spire (1749-52)
lines: Our Saviour's spiral spire (1749-52)

cards.title: A golden spiral
lines: The 90 m spire has an outside staircase turning four times around it. Approved in 1749, finished in 1752.
cards.note: Importer said 400 steps, the last 150 outside: not in S10, removed

cards.title: Frederiksstaden
lines: A new district around an octagonal square: four palaces called Amalienborg.

cards.title: Left unfinished
lines: In 1770 the plans for Frederik's Church are dropped. The church stands incomplete for decades.

cards.title: Christiansborg burns (1794)
lines: Christiansborg burns (1794)

cards.title: The palace burns
lines: Christiansborg is ruined by fire in 1794. The royal family moves to Amalienborg.

cards.title: The second fire
lines: 5 June 1795: 909 houses burn and over 6,000 people lose their homes.

cards.title: Nelson at Copenhagen
lines: On 2 April 1801 a British fleet attacks the Dano-Norwegian navy anchored off the city.

cards.title: British bombardment
lines: From 2 September the British bombard the city, with 300 Congreve rockets. About 195 civilians are killed.
cards.note: Importer said three nights: not in S23, removed

cards.title: Christiansborg II
lines: Hansen builds a second palace in a French Empire style, 1803 to 1828.

cards.title: Christiansborg rises again (1803-28)
lines: Christiansborg rises again (1803-28)

cards.title: Norway is lost
lines: The Treaty of Kiel hands Norway to Sweden and ends the union that began in 1536/37.

cards.title: Tivoli Gardens
lines: Tivoli opens on 15 August 1843 on the glacis outside the West Gate.

cards.title: A constitution
lines: 5 June 1849: the first democratic constitution ends the absolute monarchy.

cards.title: The ramparts open
lines: In the early 1850s the ramparts open and housing spreads around the Lakes.
cards.note: "Early 1850s" in S01; 1852.0 is the importer's placement

cards.title: Work restarts
lines: In 1874 the ruin is sold to Carl Frederik Tietgen, who must build a church on it.

cards.title: Nørrebro and Vesterbro
lines: New districts rise for people moving in from the provinces. The city grows from 120,000 in 1840 to 400,000 by 1901.
cards.note: Importer said "population triples in 50 years": S01 says 120,000 (1840) to 400,000 (1901)

cards.title: It burns again
lines: The second Christiansborg burns down in 1884. The ruins stand for 23 years.

cards.title: Christiansborg burns again (1884)
lines: Christiansborg burns again (1884)

cards.title: The great dome (1894)
lines: The great dome (1894)

cards.title: The dome
lines: Frederik's Church opens on 19 August 1894 with the largest church dome in Scandinavia: 31 m across.

cards.title: A bigger city
lines: Copenhagen takes in suburbs with 40,000 people. Frederiksberg becomes an enclave.

cards.title: City Hall
lines: Inaugurated on 12 September 1905. Its clock tower is 105.6 meters tall.

cards.title: The Little Mermaid
lines: Too small to see from up here: 1.25 meters. Unveiled on 23 August 1913.

cards.title: Christiansborg III
lines: The third palace, built 1907 to 1928, gets a 106 m tower: the tallest in the city.

cards.title: Christiansborg III and its tower (1907-28)
lines: Christiansborg III and its tower (1907-28)

cards.title: Grundtvig Church
lines: Yellow brick, with a west facade like a church organ. The tower church opens in 1927; work lasts until 1940.

cards.title: Occupation
lines: 9 April 1940: German troops land at the docks of Copenhagen.

cards.title: Ships sunk in the harbor
lines: In August 1943 the Danish Navy sinks several ships in the harbor so the Germans cannot use them.

cards.title: The Shellhus raid
lines: 21 March 1945: a British air raid on the Gestapo headquarters also hits a school. 123 civilians die, 87 of them schoolchildren.
cards.note: Importer said 86 children: S28 says 87 schoolchildren

cards.title: SAS Royal Hotel
lines: Arne Jacobsen's hotel opens on 1 July 1960: the first skyscraper in Copenhagen, 69.6 m.

cards.title: Christiania
lines: On 26 September 1971 squatters take over a military base and declare Freetown Christiania open.

cards.title: The Øresund Bridge
lines: Opened to traffic on 1 July 2000: road and rail connect Copenhagen and Malmö.
cards.note: Importer said 16 km: length not in the S17 segment quoted (7,845 m main link per page; not used on screen)

lines: The Opera House (2005)

cards.title: Royal Playhouse (2008)
lines: Opening year not in the fetched page text; S15 only gives the 2008 RIBA award

cards.title: The Opera House
lines: Opened on 15 January 2005, a donation to the state from the A.P. Møller foundation.

cards.title: The Royal Playhouse
lines: A theater with about 40% of the building projecting over the water.
cards.note: Opening year not in the fetched page text

cards.title: CopenHill
lines: A waste-to-energy power plant with a ski slope on its 85 m roof, opened in October 2019.

cards.title: Swimming in the harbor
lines: Today the harbor has 13 official swimming zones and three harbor baths.
cards.note: S01 states this as "now" (page fetched 2026-11); year placement 2022 is a guess

lines: 667,099 people live in the municipality. The urban area counts about 1.4 million.
cards.note: 667,099 = Wikidata P1082 2025-01-01 (Statistics Denmark BY1); not from a Wikipedia page
